diagnosis_map.notes: Disc is often passive witness. Herniation causing nerve compression = neurogenic_overload. Underlying disc matrix failure = disc_dehydration. Treat both axes.
DDD primary = disc hydration and matrix collapse. Secondary deep ligament overload compensating for disc failure = spondylosis pattern.
Neurogenic overload is primary clinical presentation. Structural disc failure is likely underlying contributor.
Spondylotic pain often comes from ligaments working too hard to compensate for failing disc-load integration. The 4th failure mode — deep ligament / segmental instability — is the primary pattern.

Facet joint pain = capsulo-ligamentous spinal pain. NOT isolated joint degeneration. NOT disc-dominant. Belongs to ligament-holding system. Sub-classify as Yin-type (hypotonic capsule) or Yang-type (hypertonic guarding). DuoLife / support agents not facet-specific — blood carries systemically.
Unclear structural source. Run failure mode scoring across 4 axes. Stasis/fascial and ligament patterns most likely when imaging is unremarkable.
Cross-reference with Batch 1 post-surgical pain module. Scarring = stasis/fascial; persisting nerve pain = shaoyang gate or hydration layer failure.
If acute/subacute: EZ continuity likely intact — steroid/block may work. If chronic: EZ fragmented — steroid fails; rebuild Yin protocol.
Radiculopathy with dermatomal spread = neurogenic_overload primary. Yang-type ligament/segmental failure often the structural driver.
Maps to Shu-Mu point logic. Organ instability → afferent overload → DRG sensitisation → CRPS-like pattern.
Taiyin collapse. Cold mitochondria pattern. Co-presents with hypotonic ligament / Yin-type spinal pattern.
Low back pain in adrenal fatigue = Yin-type spinal pattern. Cold pelvis syndrome. Warm-up protocol: Vita D/Nigella, collagen, schisandra, astragalus.
Direct analogy: spinal prolapse = pelvic prolapse at vertebral level. Qi deficiency → holding tone loss → both pelvic and spinal instability. Treat as same Yin-type pattern.
Systemic connective tissue laxity sign. Confirms Yin-type / hypotonic pattern. Same root.
Common presentation of hypotonic/Yin-type spinal pattern. Do not mobilise or stretch early. Holding tone first.
Typical TN = EZ continuous (acute/subacute). Steroid/block/PRF likely to work.
Atypical TN = EZ partially fragmented (subchronic). Mixed response to consolidation.
Neuropathic TN = EZ fragmented (chronic Yin-deficiency). Steroid fails. Rebuild Yin.

failure_mode_scoring.description: Score each failure mode 0-10 based on trigger criteria. Highest score = primary pattern. Multiple high scores = mixed pattern.

theoretical_framework_notes.summary: Universal mechanism for nerve pain: Pulse (arterial/vascular load = Liver Yang) compresses Plate (dural/perineural EZ layer) at Plexus (autonomic ganglion or DRG). Valid for both cranial (REZ + ganglion) and spinal (dural sleeve + DRG) pathways.

Exclusion zone water (EZ/structured water) in nerve sheaths, dura, and fascia = protective buffer for nerve impulse damping and regeneration. Continuity = acute/subacute; partial fragmentation = subchronic; full fragmentation = chronic Yin-deficiency. Steroid response maps directly to EZ state.

Dural system is a single continuous global EZ membrane from skull to sacrum. Sacral treatment improves trigeminal symptoms. Occiput release calms vagus. Fascia release stabilises autonomic. Treatment is never purely local.

Disc is often not the primary pain generator. Deep ligaments (PLL, ALL, flavum, facet capsules) are poorly vascularised and slow to regenerate — they generate deep, postural, diffuse pain. This is structural + microcirculatory + fascia failure. The 4-axis failure model explicitly separates disc from ligament from nerve from stasis.

Hypotonic spinal ligament = spinal prolapse. Same Qi-deficiency root as uterine prolapse, pelvic floor insufficiency, varicosities. Common in women, postpartum, chronic fatigue. Needs holding tone before movement — same sequencing as prolapse management.

Steroid classified as artificial Yang. Works when EZ continuity intact (acute/subacute). Fails when EZ fragmented (chronic/Yin-deficiency). This creates a clear clinical gating rule: assess EZ/chronicity state before steroid decision.

Facet joint pain is capsulo-ligamentous pain, not classic joint/OA pain. Pain borne by capsule + deep paraspinal fascia + ligamentous tension system, not articular surface. Apply Yin/Yang ligament sub-typing. Support agents work systemically via circulation — not facet-specific targeting needed.

Disc, ligament, and fascia are functional categories, not exclusive anatomical targets. Support acts systemically via circulation and matrix integration. Engine should score functional failure modes, not assign interventions based on anatomy alone.
